novel_features.name: Transfer risk under live delay
novel_features.description: Tells you whether the transfers in a journey still hold once today's delays are applied.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining per-leg live delay from the connections endpoint against official_transfer_time from the open stations dataset, which the API itself never exposes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of a plain route lookup whenever a journey has a transfer and delays are already in play.
novel_features.group: Live data joined with open datasets

novel_features.name: Route punctuality history
novel_features.description: Shows how reliable a train or route has actually been, from delay observations recorded on your machine.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local observation store; every existing Belgian rail tool is stateless and discards each response after printing it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for questions about the past such as chronic lateness; it never calls the API.

novel_features.name: Disruptions scoped to one journey
novel_features.description: Filters the national disruption feed down to the stations your journey actually passes through.
novel_features.rationale: Requires resolving the stations on a route and matching them against free-text disruption titles, which no tool does and the API cannot do server-side.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when the national list is too noisy to answer whether one specific trip is affected.
novel_features.group: Live data joined with open datasets

novel_features.name: Live observation capture
novel_features.description: Records what the board says right now into local SQLite, building the history other commands read.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local store; the API offers no historical endpoint and no client keeps observations.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this on a schedule; it is what makes punctuality and changes able to answer anything.

novel_features.name: Latest safe departure
novel_features.description: Answers the last train you can take and still arrive before a deadline, accounting for current delays.
novel_features.rationale: Requires arrival-based planning plus live delay math and a safety margin, rather than the raw arrival-time query the API provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when the arrival deadline is fixed and the departure time is the unknown.

novel_features.name: Station facilities and accessibility
novel_features.description: Reports step-free access, elevators, ramps, lockers, bike parking and ticket-desk hours for a station.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the open facilities dataset, which is published separately and is absent from the API's own station response.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for accessibility and amenity questions that the live rail API simply cannot answer.
novel_features.group: Live data joined with open datasets

novel_features.name: What changed since last check
novel_features.description: Reports new delays, cancellations and platform changes since the last time you looked.
novel_features.rationale: Requires diffing consecutive local observations, including a platform-change flag that is present in live responses but absent from the published docs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for deltas during a commute rather than re-reading a whole board.

narrative.headline: Every Belgian rail lookup the existing tools offer, plus transfer-risk, delay history and accessibility data that none of them have.
narrative.value_prop: iRail exposes live NMBS/SNCB departures, journey planning and disruptions for free with no API key. This CLI adds what every other client throws away: it records observations locally so punctuality can answer whether a train is chronically late, joins the open stations dataset so transfer-risk knows the real minimum transfer time at each station, and surfaces station accessibility data the API never returns. The analysis commands emit typed JSON - delays as numbers, cancellations as booleans - while the raw endpoint commands pass iRail's payload through unchanged.
narrative.auth_narrative: No credentials are required: the iRail API is open and unauthenticated, so every command works immediately after install. Two operational limits matter instead of a key. iRail allows 3 requests per second per IP with 5 burst, returning HTTP 429 beyond that, so this CLI ships an adaptive rate limiter. iRail also blocks source IPs that send no User-Agent without prior warning, so every request carries an identifying User-Agent automatically.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the binary works and the API is reachable; no credentials needed
Pull the 716-station reference set into local SQLite; board and route are live-only and take no sync
The core lookup: what is leaving right now, with delay and platform
Plan a journey with transfers and per-leg live delay
Narrow the national disruption feed to just this journey
Start recording observations so punctuality and changes have history to read

troubleshoots.fix: iRail allows 3 requests/second per IP plus 5 burst. Reduce concurrency or add --limit to narrow the query; the built-in limiter backs off automatically.

troubleshoots.symptom: Requests suddenly fail from your network
troubleshoots.fix: iRail blocks IPs that send no User-Agent. Do not strip the User-Agent header; if already blocked, contact the iRail team to be unblocked.

troubleshoots.symptom: Output is XML instead of JSON
troubleshoots.fix: The API defaults to xml. This CLI always sends format=json; if you overrode it, drop --format or set --format json.

troubleshoots.symptom: train get returns today even though you passed a date
troubleshoots.fix: Upstream ignores the date parameter on the vehicle endpoint. Use board list with --date to inspect another day.

troubleshoots.symptom: HTTP 500 on a date far in the past or future
troubleshoots.fix: iRail only holds a window around the current date. Query a date close to today.
Both read local observations. Run irail-pp-cli observe at least twice before expecting results.

troubleshoots.symptom: A station name is not recognised
troubleshoots.fix: Run irail-pp-cli stations search with part of the name; it matches Dutch, French, German and English names plus telegraph codes such as FBMZ.

troubleshoots.symptom: delay or canceled compares wrong in jq, e.g. .delay > 300 is always false
troubleshoots.fix: The raw endpoint commands (board, route, stations, disruptions, train) return iRail's payload verbatim, and iRail encodes every scalar as a string. Cast with (.delay|tonumber), or use the analysis commands (transfer-risk, punctuality, leave-by, changes, observe) which emit typed numbers and booleans.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for anything involving Belgian passenger rail: when the next train leaves, how to get from one station to another, whether a journey is disrupted, and how reliable a route has been over time. It is the right tool when you need typed, scriptable output rather than a web page, and the only tool that can answer historical punctuality or transfer-risk questions. It also serves accessibility questions about Belgian stations that the live API cannot answer.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to buy tickets, reserve seats or check fares; iRail is a read-only timetable API with no booking surface.
Do not use it for rail networks outside Belgium; coverage is NMBS/SNCB plus a small number of cross-border stations.
Do not use it for live vehicle GPS positions; the API reports scheduled and delayed times, not continuous tracking.
Do not use it to query personal NMBS account data such as subscriptions or order history; that lives behind belgiantrain.be, which this CLI does not touch.

recipes.title: Next departures, narrowed for an agent
recipes.explanation: A full board is roughly 34 KB of JSON; selecting four fields keeps the response small enough to reason over without burning context.

recipes.title: Will my transfer survive today's delays
recipes.explanation: Joins live per-leg delay against each station's official minimum transfer time and flags transfers that no longer hold.

recipes.title: Only the disruptions that affect my commute
recipes.explanation: Filters the national feed, which was 32 entries on a normal day, down to the stations this journey passes through.

recipes.title: Last train that still gets me there by nine
recipes.explanation: Plans backwards from the deadline and applies current delays plus a safety margin.

recipes.title: Is this station step-free
recipes.explanation: Reads the open facilities dataset for elevators, ramps and wheelchair access, none of which the rail API returns.

trigger_phrases: when is my train to Ghent
are there any rail disruptions in Belgium
plan a train journey from Leuven to Antwerp
